Final Works Begin on Southern Bacău Interchange as A7 Bypass Closes for Two Weeks Deșteptarea 17 august 2026 se citește în 2 min. Acțiune Facebook X WhatsApp Telegram VK Construction of the southern Bacău road interchange has entered its final phase, with contractors preparing to connect the Bacău bypass section of the A7 motorway to newly built stretches of the Moldova Motorway, local authorities said on Monday. According to officials, road infrastructure near the existing bypass and the interchange ramps is ready for the final connection works. Road markings have already been completed and safety barriers installed, while crews are currently carrying out embankment works, concreting hydrocarbon separators and installing the lighting system. To allow the final tie-in works, the A7 Bacău Bypass will be fully closed to traffic between Aug. 17 and Aug. 31 , starting at 7:00 a.m. local time on Monday . The closure was approved at the request of the contractor under a joint authorization issued by Romania’s National Road Infrastructure Administration Company (CNAIR) and the Romanian Police Inspectorate (IGPR). The traffic restrictions cover the entire bypass, between its junction with National Road DN2 at the southern entrance to Bacău from Nicolae Bălcescu commune (km 279+650) and the DN2 intersection in the Bogdan Vodă area (km 296+400). During the closure, all traffic will be diverted through Bacău via DN2. Authorities urged motorists to plan their journeys in advance and use the recommended alternative routes to avoid congestion and reduce travel times. Drivers travelling from Bucharest towards Suceava have been advised to use either the DN2–DJ252D–DJ252B–DJ252–DN2F–Calea Bârladului–Calea Romanului–DN2 route or the DN2–DN2T–DN11–Arcadie Șeptilici Street–DN2G–DJ119B–DN15–DN2U–DN2 route. Traffic heading towards Vaslui will be diverted via DN2–DJ252D–DJ252B–DJ252–DN2F, while motorists travelling to Piatra Neamț are advised to follow the DN2–DN2T–DN11–Arcadie Șeptilici Street–DN2G–DJ119B–DN15 route. Background The Bacău Bypass is one of the key components of Romania’s A7 Moldova Motorway , the country’s largest motorway project currently under construction. The A7 is designed to improve north-south connectivity in eastern Romania, linking Ploiești with the northern regions near the Ukrainian border and significantly reducing transit traffic through major cities. Construction is currently focused on completing the final section of the Focșani–Bacău motorway between Răcăciuni and Bacău, as well as all three lots of the Bacău–Pașcani section. Once completed, the new motorway is expected to improve freight transport, shorten travel times and strengthen connections between Moldova and the rest of Romania. https://www.middlenecknews.com/local-new.text: The Montross Town Council has changed vendors for a required water withdrawal report after finding a less expensive option. The town had approved a vendor at an estimated cost of 24 thousand 700 dollars, but later received a bid from another vendor that was about 10 thousand dollars cheaper. That particular vendor has also prepared similar reports for Warsaw for roughly 20 years. Council members unanimously approved the change, calling it a significant savings for the town.

https://www.bursa.ro/ubb-obtains-first-e.text: The Babeş-Bolyai University of Cluj-Napoca (UBB) has obtained a grant of almost 1.5 million euros from the European Research Council (ERC), within the Starting Grant competition, for a project dedicated to the relationship between unconscious processes and conscious experience. According to the university, the funding represents a first for psychology in Romania. *Five-year funded research The project, entitled GENESIS - "Hidden in Plain Sight: The Genesis of Conscious Experience from Statistical Regularities”, is coordinated by lect. univ. dr. Răzvan Jurchiş, from the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences of UBB. The university specifies that the project received an A grade in the ERC Starting Grant competition, and the requested amount, of 1,489,715 euros, was granted in full. The research will be carried out over a period of five years. The ERC Starting Grants are intended for researchers at the beginning of their independent careers and are awarded following a European competition focused on scientific excellence. According to UBB, it is the first ERC grant obtained by a Romanian institution in the field of psychology since the establishment of the European Research Council in 2007. *How does unconscious information become conscious experience The GENESIS project starts from one of the fundamental questions of psychology and cognitive science: how does what we learn without realizing it become part of our conscious experience? The researchers' hypothesis is that conscious experience may arise through a process of information compression. Complex structures learned unconsciously would be transformed by the mind into simpler and more easily accessible conscious representations. This hypothesis may explain situations in which people use information that they are not able to explain consciously. UBB offers as examples the grammatical rules used by speakers of a language without them being able to formulate them explicitly or the movements performed by athletes without each stage of a sequence being able to be described verbally. "What we think we know about the reasons for our own actions may not always faithfully reflect the processes that actually guided our behavior,” explained Răzvan Jurchiş, the project coordinator. The research will follow, starting from this premise, how regularities and structures learned unconsciously are transformed into conscious representations. *A first for Romanian psychology For UBB, obtaining the grant represents both a recognition of the project and the researcher who coordinates it, and an indicator of the university's ability to compete for high-level European funding. "An ERC grant represents one of the strongest such validations,” declared the UBB rector, prof. univ. dr. psych. Daniel David, who emphasized that the research topic continues a direction developed by the Cluj school of psychology in the field of unconscious information processing. European funding will allow the development, over the next five years, of a research program dedicated to the relationship between unconscious processes and conscious experience. At the same time, according to UBB, the project will contribute to strengthening the participation of Romanian research in leading international networks in psychology and cognitive sciences. Photograph: Ken Urker via Instagram Louisiana Partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard found dead in Louisiana home Kenan ‘Ken’ Urker, 34, who died of apparent drug overdose, was partner of woman convicted of murder of mother Marina Dunbar Fri 2 Oct 2026 19.53 EDT First published on Fri 2 Oct 2026 18.24 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The on-and-off partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard , who spent time in prison for her role in the murder of her abusive mother, was found dead inside his Louisiana home on his 34th birthday on Thursday in what authorities described as an apparent drug overdose. The sheriff’s office in Lafourche parish, Louisiana , confirmed Kenan “Ken” Urker – the father of Blanchard’s daughter – was discovered on Thursday after relatives asked police to conduct a welfare check at his residence. According to a sheriff’s office report on the case, Anita Blanchard said she and her husband – who is Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s half-brother – went to Urker’s home and saw him lying unconscious through an outside window. A man who was with the couple then entered the house through a window and found Urker unresponsive. The sheriff’s office report obtained by the Guardian states that Urker was not breathing and was “cold to the touch”. Authorities who arrived at the scene were “able to see Mr Urker from the living room area lying on his back in [a] bed”, the report said. Deputies reported that they then walked in the direction of the room where the bed was “and located paraphernalia (syringes and spoon) in the bathroom next to a brown powdery substance”. Authorities also found a syringe and a handgun on the nightstand beside the bed. Besides being cold to the touch, Urker “appeared to have been there for an extended period of time”. In an interview with People published on Friday, the 32-year-old Gypsy Rose Blanchard said that she believed Urker died from an overdose – though she said she did not know whether it was deliberate. “I don’t know if it was intentional or not,” Blanchard said, adding that Urker “was not in a good state of mind lately”. In a statement published to her Instagram story on Friday, Blanchard said Urker “endured an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying across social media platforms, including TikTok and Reddit”. “The cruelty directed toward him was something no human being should have to endure,” Blanchard wrote. “I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him, and I hope his passing serves as a reminder that there is a real person behind every screen, every headline, and every comment.” The sheriff’s office report on Urker’s death confirmed the case had been called in to the agency as an evident overdose. In a statement to the news media, Brennan Matherne, the Lafourche parish sheriff’s captain, said Urker’s death remained “under investigation” as of Friday. Matherne also said investigators as of Friday had not discovered “any signs of foul play”. Blanchard previously spent eight years in prison after being convicted of second-degree murder in connection with the 2015 stabbing death of her mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard. Dee Dee Blanchard was found stabbed to death in her home in Springfield, Missouri , in June 2015. Gypsy Rose Blanchard had provided her then boyfriend, Nicholas Godejohn, with a knife and hid in a bathroom while he killed her mother. Blanchard pleaded guilty to second-degree murder. Godejohn, whom Blanchard met online, was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. Dee Dee Blanchard’s murder drew widespread attention after it was revealed that she had forced Gypsy Rose to pretend she was seriously ill and undergo medical procedures she did not need. Blanchard met Urker while serving her prison sentence, from which she was released in late December 2023. She said on the We Need to Talk podcast in June that Urker had contacted her after watching Mommy Dead and Dearest , a 2017 documentary about Gypsy Rose and Dee Dee. As Gypsy Rose put it, Urker sent her a “supportive letter, not on any kind of romantic level” and included his phone number. Urker proposed in October 2018. The pair later ended their engagement before reuniting in August 2019. They eventually split again and spent several years apart. During that time, Blanchard married Ryan Anderson. Anderson and Blanchard later separated, with her announcing the split four months after her release from prison. Blanchard and Urker rekindled their relationship in April 2024. Eight months later, they welcomed their daughter, Aurora Raina Urker.
